radiology_report:
Spaarne Gasthuis (Haarlem)
Radiology Dept
Date: 20 Jan 2025
Exam: mpMRI prostate

Clinical indication: Rising PSA (190.0 ng/mL), prior biopsy Gleason 4+3, ISUP GG3.

FINDINGS:
The prostate measures 46.38 mL in volume. T2-weighted imaging reveals a dominant, ill-defined hypo-intense lesion within the left apical peripheral zone, measuring approximately 18 mm in craniocaudal dimension. On diffusion-weighted imaging, this region demonstrates marked restricted diffusion with corresponding low apparent diffusion coefficient values. Dynamic contrast-enhanced sequences show early, intense focal enhancement corresponding to the DWI/T2 abnormality. No evidence of extracapsular extension, seminal vesicle invasion, or pelvic lymphadenopathy is identified.

IMPRESSION:
PI-RADS 5 lesion in the left apical peripheral zone.
PSA density 4.097 ng/mL/mL.
Clinical T stage cT1c.
csPCa predicted probability 0.9718793.

previous_notes.author: Dr. R. Visser (GP)
previous_notes.text: Patient presented with a PSA of 7.0 ng/mL, an increase from the baseline of 3.0 ng/mL recorded in July 2022. Digital rectal examination was unremarkable. An mpMRI was arranged, and a transrectal ultrasound-guided biopsy was subsequently performed.

pathology_report:
Biopsy 1 (Aug 2023): The histological assessment demonstrates adenocarcinoma with mostly moderately to poorly formed tubules that often fuse and regularly form cribriform areas. Also, quite a few well-formed tubules. The Gleason score is 4+3, corresponding to ISUP grade group 3. A cribriform pattern is present. Perineural invasion is confirmed. The tumour is located in the peripheral zone, apical left.

Trajectory summary: The disease has remained consistent at ISUP grade group 3 across the single documented biopsy timepoint.

AI-predicted ISUP grade group (digital pathology): grade group 4.
